chunks: Now, the trust has been returned and what had been given has been taken back.
As to my grief, it knows no bounds, and as to my nights, they will remain sleepless till Allāh chooses for me the house in which you are now residing.

Certainly, your daughter would apprise you of the joining together of your ummah (people) for oppressing her. You ask her in detail and get all the news about the position. This has happened when a long time had not elapsed and your remembrance had not disappeared.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his grief and the future oppression of his family after Fatimah's death?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) reflects on the usurpation of Fatimah’s dowry (al-wadi'ah) and the taking of her pledge (al-rahinah), key events in Shia historiography regarding the early Caliphate. He contrasts his eternal sorrow and sleepless nights with the anticipation of divine retribution, while prophesying that his daughter Zaynab will report the community's collective oppression (tahammul) against their household. This passage underscores the transition from private grief to public political consciousness, highlighting the enduring legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.
